name: criterion-contestability-boundary
purpose: Prevent upstream relevance selection, framing, orientation, or trajectory construction from silently acquiring consequence-bearing authority.

definitions.orientation: A source-bound frame, criterion, distinction, or trajectory that shapes what becomes actionable.
definitions.contestability: The property that a criterion remains visible and challengeable through the consequence boundary.
definitions.admissibility: A separate present-tense determination that a consequence-bearing transition may cross the commit boundary.

invariants: orientation MUST NOT be treated as execution authority
contestability MUST NOT be treated as admissibility
parallel trajectories MUST NOT be collapsed into synthetic consensus as a substitute for authority
criterion provenance MUST remain bound for consequence-bearing transitions
criterion contestability MUST remain available at the consequence boundary
criterion authority MUST be independently current at the consequence boundary
relations among consequence-bearing trajectories MUST be governed
successful planning or execution MUST NOT repair an inadmissible upstream criterion
unresolved required evidence MUST defer rather than invent authority

composition.rule: CCB-001 adds upstream criterion/frame predicates without modifying PA-001 or treating PA-001 permission as authority.
